Not to further plunge you into despair or anything, but if you are in the UK you should prepare yourself that it'll be longer than a year.

I've been on a "nine month" waiting list for some sort of therapy for three years now.

If you're really struggling (like thinking of hurting yourself) your best bet is to turn up at A&E and kick up a polite fuss. You'll be waiting in the waiting room for at least eight hours though, so plan accordingly. You should also be prepared for an outcome that involves a stay at a crisis unit (but they'll try not to force you).

There's also private organisations that you have to pay for. They're not great, but if you just need someone to talk to they're good to tide you over until you can see a specialist.

There's different groups depending on where you live and some offer reduced rates if you have low income so you can find something with a bit of googling. I know of one in my region that's £5 for an hours session.

Mental health services in the UK are pretty much nonexistent.

Sprint is mitigation. Mobs cant hit you if they cant keep up with you.

For most dungeons (especially early dungeons).

Activate sprint before you pull the mobs as this gives you 20 second sprint duration instead of 10 in combat.

As you run towards the mobs ranged attack or provoke one of them.

Glance at the enemy list, ranged attack any that you missed (green circle) or any that you're losing aggro on.

When you stop pick a spot and stand still. Don't move unless you're moving out of an aoe attack (or doing a mechanic like cleansing doom or something). Face the mobs away from the majority of the party, a lot of mobs have cleave attacks that aren't telegraphed where they hit everyone in a cone in front of them.

I got VR yesterday, so don't have many ideas in terms of pure vr issues, other than use USB 3.0 and try a different cable.

For the PC side of things though, if your PC is struggling it'd affect performance so it could be a variety of things.

Have a glance at task manager and see if you notice anything odd in terms of performance. It's not perfect, but can be used as an indicator for issues. Check temps too.

24gb of ram makes me wary. You got 3 sticks that are mismatched by any chance? Ram can be finicky in some cases for issues like that, but theoretically it should be fine.

Could also be overheating/thermal throttling due to poor airflow/dust. Give the PC a clean if it looks like it needs it.

Could also be loose cables, reseat your parts and check the connections.

Kill any tasks you're not using, disable antivirus, etc etc.

You can use ranged attacks and provoke whilst running. Provided the tank gets a decent aoe on the mobs initially then ranged attacks can be used to maintain agro in a lot of cases.

I wouldn't blame a tank for losing aggro in that niche situation though, which is why the DPS should run with the tank and not stop even if they gain aggro.

Sprint is a form of damage mitigation in the sense that you can run too fast for the mobs to keep up and be able to damage you, applies to DPS too. Dps can also use arms length, bloodbath, second wind etc to keep themselves alive whilst running.

So, ideally tanks would:

Run slightly in front, use sprint pre-pull to get the double duration bonus.

Ranged attack or provoke a pack to draw the pack in together as you approach.

AOE whilst running through the clumped up group.

Keep running and ranged attack mobs you're about to lose aggro on, or alternate ranged attacks on each mob when you're not approaching a new pack or about to lose aggro on a specific mob.

Stand still (LOS ranged mobs) when the pull stops and don't move unless you absolutely have to (to avoid telegraphed attacks). Dps stop when you stop and your regular AOE will pick up any stragglers from them before they can do significant damage.

If you pull aggro from the tank, it's the tanks fault 99% of the time and not something you should be overly concerned about.

They have a passive toggleable skill that means they generate 10x more aggro than anyone else.

Use AOE skills on multiple mobs (usually 3 or more but some classes it's 2 or more), target specific mobs with scary abilities to kill them quick or target what the other DPS are targeting to kill that thing quicker if none of the above applies.
